profile.reading:
This facility is ADP's Sioux Falls, South Dakota campus at 4915 North Marion Road, on the city's north side. Minnehaha County property records identify the parcel by the legal description "Lot 1 Block 1 ADP Addition," meaning the surrounding subdivision itself was platted under ADP's name, a strong indication that the company developed the site as a purpose-built campus rather than leasing space in a shared building. County and commercial-listing records describe a 195,113-square-foot building on 34.68 acres, classified under a light-manufacturing land-use code, sitting on Parcel ID 78115. The Sioux Falls Area Chamber of Commerce has listed ADP at this same address since at least 2007, categorized under payroll and payment-processing services.

ADP, Automatic Data Processing, Inc., is one of the largest payroll, human-capital-management, and tax-processing companies in the country, running paychecks, benefits administration, and compliance systems for employers nationwide. A campus of this size is consistent with a major regional processing and operations center rather than a small branch office, and facilities of this kind for large payroll processors typically combine office space for HR and support staff with server rooms or data halls that run the underlying payroll and compliance systems, though ADP's public materials do not specifically confirm which functions are housed in the Sioux Falls building, or break out how much of its footprint, if any, is dedicated data center space as opposed to office and operations use.

Sioux Falls has a long history as a back-office and data-processing hub for national financial and consumer-services companies, owing to South Dakota's favorable tax structure, central time zone, and relatively low utility costs; Citibank's credit card operations, for instance, have anchored a similar cluster of large processing campuses in the same metro area for decades. ADP's Sioux Falls facility fits that broader pattern of large employers running back-office and technical infrastructure from the region rather than from higher-cost coastal markets.

As with most enterprise-owned, non-colocation data infrastructure, ADP does not publish IT capacity, power draw, cooling design, or redundancy specifications for this or any other of its facilities: the building exists to run ADP's own systems rather than to be marketed to outside tenants, so there is no commercial reason for ADP to disclose the kind of technical specification sheet a wholesale colocation provider would. What is publicly confirmable is the address, the scale of the platted campus, and ADP's long-standing occupancy of it.
